info.title: Pramaan API
info.description: Provider-neutral capabilities behind one API. Prices are in micro-USD.

requires_approval.description: Present on an action that moves money, reaches, calls, checks or locks out a real person: have a person approve each call before you run it.

result_once.description: The result is returned once, is not stored, and cannot be replayed. Call directly from your own code; model-facing tools refuse it.

price_ceiling_micro.description: The most one call is priced at, micro-USD, unless the request sends its own limit in Pramaan-Max-Price-Micro.

effect.description: Present when nothing was sent, charged or created: every source refused before acting, or the request was refused before anything ran (validation, approval, balance, limits). Absent when anything may have happened: check before retrying an action.

required_micro.description: With `spend_cap_reached`: the most the request can cost, micro-USD.

reason.description: With `spend_cap_reached`: not enough credit, the daily spend cap, or the spending limit of the member the call acts as. With `forbidden`: `approval_required`, the call needs an approver (send `Pramaan-Approved-By`).

plan.description: With `approval_required` on an outcome: the plan to show a person, then send in `Pramaan-Plan`.

needs.description: With `approval_required` on an outcome: the steps that ask a person to approve.

result.description: The capability's result once the job is done. A bulk run you cancelled keeps the rows already answered here (the ones you were charged for).

effect.description: Present when the job failed before anything was sent, charged or created.

progress.description: Only while a bulk run is running: how far it is.

charged_micro.description: What this job has been charged so far, micro-USD. It moves from 0 to the job's price when the job is settled, and stays 0 for a job that was refused or failed and charged nothing. Absent on a long outcome run: its money is its result's `cost`.

held_micro.description: Credit still set aside for this job, micro-USD: the estimate taken at the start while it runs, 0 once the job has finished. Absent on a long outcome run: its money is its result's `cost`.

version.description: Send it back in If-Match when you save.

capability.description: A family ("payments.*") or one capability id.

country.description: Country code(s) of the payer or recipient; EU, EEA, GCC expand when saved.

name.description: The display name, or null while none is set.

held_micro.description: The credit set aside for the job (its estimate), micro-USD; 0 when it takes none. Not a price: what the job is charged reads on GET /v1/jobs/{id} once it is settled.

read_only_key.description: True when the calling key may only run read_only capabilities.

effect_class.description: The highest effect class among the steps it may run.

mode.description: async: the run answers 202 with a job; poll GET /v1/jobs/{id}.

price_max_micro.description: The most a run can cost with every step on, micro-USD.

post.summary: Upload a file to pass to a capability as `fileId`
post.description:
Send the file as the request body, with its media type in `Content-Type`.

The file is kept 7 days. Uploads are free; you can hold up to 1 GB at a time.

This endpoint accepts at most 90 MB (images 20 MB). For larger files, POST /v1/files/uploads, PUT bytes to uploadUrl using the returned headers, then POST /v1/files/{id}/finish. Direct limits: audio, document and data 100 MB; video 500 MB.

`kind=part` is one part of a multipart upload: raw bytes sent as `application/octet-stream`, at most 8 MiB. A part can only be passed to `storage.upload.part.put`. It has no link and is deleted when its upload completes or is aborted.

post.summary: What a request would cost at most, without running it
post.description: Send the same body (and the same Pramaan-Max-Price-Micro and Pramaan-Second-Opinion headers) you would send to the capability. Nothing runs, nothing is charged or set aside, and no Idempotency-Key is used. price_typical_micro is a cached cross-caller median, not the hold. Bounds follow the validated request: llm.complete defaults maxTokens to 4096; character-priced translation follows input length, while fixed-price sources retain their full call price; a single video reserves one routed call, including its enforced route cap.

schema.description: Optional. The most this request may be priced at, in micro-USD (a whole number above 0). It replaces the capability's own price ceiling for this request, lower or higher. Sources that could cost more are left out; when none is left the answer is 400 with the lowest limit that would work.

parameters.description: Optional. The most this request may be priced at, in micro-USD (a whole number above 0). It replaces the capability's own price ceiling for this request, lower or higher. get.summary: The people in your organisation, with their roles
get.description:
A client that acts for people (a chat app) maps its users to these members.

Any call can act as one member of your organisation: send `Pramaan-Member: <member_id>`. A key made for one member always acts as them. The call then runs with that member's role (a viewer only reads; a member runs capabilities; admins and the owner do everything), counts toward their spending limit (402 `member_limit` when it is reached) and is recorded as theirs.

A call made as a member that asks a person to approve it, or costs more than your approval threshold, runs only with an approver: the member themselves when they may approve, or `Pramaan-Approved-By: <member_id>` naming one who did. Otherwise it is refused with 403 `forbidden`.

Members are managed in the dashboard.

may_approve.description: Whether `Pramaan-Approved-By` may name them now: the owner, a member with the approval flag, or an admin when admins approve.

get.summary: Your organisation and its display name
get.description: The organisation of the key that asks. The display name is what a person outside the platform is shown as who is contacting them (a candidate's invitation, for example). Until you set one, `name` is null and a neutral label is shown instead.

default.description: Error (see the error guide for codes)

put.description:
Only an owner or an admin may set it: a call acting as a member or a viewer is refused with 403 `forbidden`. A key that acts as no member acts as the organisation and may.

The name is trimmed and its spaces collapsed, then must be 2 to 200 characters, with no control or invisible characters. It may not contain an email address, be a web address, be the default name, or be only a generic word such as `support`, `security` or `bank`. A refused name is `invalid_request`; the message names the rule and never repeats the name.

Setting the same name again changes nothing. Changes are limited to about 10 a day for one organisation (429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`), and each change is recorded with who made it.

Nothing is sent anywhere by this call. Something already created for your organisation at a service before the name was set keeps its earlier label unless that service can rename it.

price_typical_micro.description: Sum of active steps' capability medians times their planned maximum call counts, each capped at its step's bound, then kept between price_min_micro and price_max_micro. Each paid step needs at least 20 successful paid calls among its last 200 within 30 days across all callers; otherwise omitted. Cached for 5 minutes. Historical guidance only; does not change the hold.
